items.q: What's the first step in building evals for an agent?
items.a: **Break the job into discrete tasks** and define what success looks like with the people who do it today.

items.q: How do you eval an agent with no users yet?
items.a: Build **synthetic worlds**—a fake company with its full data—and rerun the agent on the same frozen state as a **backtest**.

items.q: What did Ramp grade: the path or the result?
items.a: The **final output** against 10-20 criteria, plus **cost and latency**—not which tools were called.
Accuracy gives **partial credit**; pass@k is **all-or-nothing** across criteria.
When one wrong step **destroys trust**, like closing the books.

items.q: How do you find skills to cut?
items.a: **Skill ablation**: leave one out, rerun, and delete or compress skills that don't move the score.

items.q: How did Ramp test agent memory?
items.a: With **roll-forward worlds**: the period-1 run writes memory, the period-2 run reads it—one of the **biggest gains**.

items.q: Did auto-tuning prompts in text space help?
items.a: No—Ramp saw **no gain**; there's no real gradient to climb.

items.q: Why not gate CI on agent evals?
items.a: They're too **non-deterministic**; run **scheduled regression** and let an agent triage failures to Slack.
